fun_highlights: The callback system is the game's single best mechanic: when 'cb_books_late' fires because you kept the book at age 9, or 'cb_outcast_return' pays back a childhood kindness 21 years later, the long arc closing feels genuinely earned — not scripted. These moments are the reason to play another life.

Vocation branching works. A soldier's life and a scholar's life are structurally different enough that the adult band reads differently: war-PTSD cards, the 'frail body bill' for soldiers vs. 'does the scholar's wager pay off' — the four callings are real divergences, not just flavour text on the same beats.
Era variety (war/plague/plenty/hard/turning) visibly changes what childhood opens on and which rare cards can fire. Arriving into a plague year versus fat years is felt, not just labelled.

Dynasty-layer rewards are genuinely satisfying: a motto crystallising mid-generation, a house-standing rise you caused by investment, a secret passing down through three lives — these make the player feel like they're playing a long game, not just watching a loop.

The prose pool is wide enough that individual lines rarely repeat within a session. The anti-staleness machinery (RECENT_LINES, per-dynasty RECENT, cluster-blocking in epitaphFor) is real and mostly works across 15 dynasties.

The 'inherited secret' and 'family shadow' mechanics (repute-gated cards, tainted reputation gating) make a ruthless house feel different to inhabit than a scholarly one — there are doors a disgraced name will never open.
staleness: The structural skeleton of almost every life is identical across all 15 dynasties: origin card (age 3-5) → book or stray or sibling (age 6-12) → calling fork at 14-22 → late love (30-51) → marriage → child → work/trade midlife card → elder body/legacy/bequest → die. The player sees the same spine every single time. By dynasty 6-8 this is fully visible and the meditative pace makes it harder to ignore, not easier.

Late love is far too dominant as the default romantic arc. Scanning the transcripts: Dynasties 1, 3, 5, 6 (Emory), 7, 8 (Annika), 9, 11 (Vera, Tobias), 12 (Junia), 13 (Ottilie), 14 (Tariq) — nearly every founder and many heirs fall in love in their 30s-50s via 'a_meet_late' or late-nudged 'y_love1'. The fix was to spread love across ages, but the transcripts show the most common shape is still: no youth love → late love in 30s-40s → child close to 50. Dynasty 2 (Vera, age 23) and Dynasty 14 (Tariq, age 18) are the exceptions. The 'lapsed player' notices this hardening into a template.

Several individual cards recur in almost every playthrough because they're not 'once-per-dynasty': 'a_marry' and the marriage beat lands identically phrased in 12 of 15 dynasties, 'u_loss' and 'u_windfall' recur with minimal variation, the 'cb_principle' re-stand fires in Dynasties 1, 9, 11, 13, 14, 15 all with near-identical phrasing ('Paid, a second time and more dearly, for a principle he would not set down'). The text variants exist but the same lines dominate.

Midlife is the thinnest band structurally. Adult cards are plentiful (26 ids) but midlife only has 18, and several are heavily conditional. Most midlife sections in the transcripts run: parent-aging card OR work offer → m_health OR m_money → maybe one repute-gated card → bequest → done. It reads as a compressed slide toward death rather than a full life-stage.

The 'one more dynasty' pull is present in abstract (the aspiration list, building toward seat-7, a motto not yet crystallised) but the dynasty layer does not produce enough player-legible surprise. Rising from 'a rented room' to 'a comfortable household' across four generations is satisfying once; the second time it's a slower repeat of the same climb. There are no dramatically different dynasty archetypes — no way a ruthless house plays out through multiple generations that feels fundamentally unlike a scholarly one in the mid-game.

Lives that stay solitary (no spouse, no children) are mechanically thin: Dynasties 4 (Ingrid), 5 (Elias), 9 (Marguerite), 10 (Lazlo) all end without an heir or spouse and their transcripts are noticeably shorter and more repetitive in the elder band, because many elder cards require a spouse or child as a condition. A deliberately childless or solitary run is under-supported with late content.

improvements.what: Break the spine earlier: introduce 2-3 structural forks that change which mid-band a life enters, before the calling card. E.g., a childhood 'fortune/crisis' that sets the house to 'poor' or 'comfortable' opening, which then gates different adult clusters rather than just adjusting stats.
improvements.why: Right now every life's first 30 years run child-pool → calling → love → marriage. The spine is identical regardless of choices because the calling only diverges the life after it fires. Starting structural divergence at age 6-12 would mean two lives genuinely start from different places, not different prose on the same shape.

improvements.what: Add 3-4 'shape cards' that are mutually exclusive and each redirect the adult band: e.g., 'took monastic vows' (kills marriage/child arc entirely, opens a different midlife cluster), 'became itinerant' (unlocks wanderer-specific mid/elder cards), 'inherited an obligation' (gates a duty-vs-freedom cluster for adult). These are not more choices; they are different life shapes.
improvements.why: The lapsed player's complaint is not 'not enough cards' — it's 'same template with new paint.' Shape cards would mean a player who takes vows genuinely has a different structural arc for 50 years, not just different stat outcomes from the same beat sequence.

improvements.what: Spread love across ages more aggressively. Make youth love (y_love1) fire with high probability before age 21 for a majority of non-once-per-dynasty founders; make late love genuinely rare (15-20% of lives, not 65%). Give youth-married lives a distinct set of adult complications (early parenthood pressures, growing-apart cards, a 'married too young' callback) that late-love lives never see.
improvements.why: In the transcripts, the 'late love across an ordinary Tuesday — someone' phrasing lands in 10+ dynasties at ages 30-52. It is now the default template, not the poignant exception. The intended structural variety (early love vs. late love vs. solitary) is not realised in practice.

improvements.what: Expand and gate the solitary/childless life. Add 8-10 elder and midlife cards that only fire when no spouse and no child exist: chosen solitude moments, the relationship with work or craft as the primary bond, a 'made family of chosen people' arc that has its own bequest card, late-found companionship of a non-romantic kind. Currently a solitary run has a visibly shorter and more repetitive log.
improvements.why: A deliberate 'no family' run is a real life shape that the game acknowledges but doesn't support with commensurate content. When it becomes a legitimate third structural path (not a foreclosed domestic arc), it adds replay value without requiring a full new card set.

improvements.what: Give the dynasty layer 2-3 more legible 'house events' that fire once per dynasty at dramatic moments: a great windfall that changes the house overnight, a catastrophe that collapses standing by 2 seats and forces a recovery arc, a generation that inherits a secret and must decide whether the dynasty pivots. These should be in the log, named in the flow, and feel like turning points — not just stat updates discovered at the heir screen.
improvements.why: The dynasty rises and falls quietly. 'The family climbed in the world this generation' is noted but not dramatised. A dynasty-level event that visibly shapes the next life's circumstances (born into the ruins of a great house, or into unexpected windfall) would create the 'story I didn't expect' that defines the best narrative-sim sessions.

verdict: A Life is beautifully made and genuinely does some things well — the callback system, vocation branching, and dynasty-layer accumulation are real pleasures — but the structural skeleton of nearly every life is the same, late love is the default rather than the exception, and by dynasty 6-8 the lapsed player is watching the same template in different prose, which is exactly what drove them away the first time.
